Well, one of the few houses we could see from the highway had recently been on fire.

Anyway, we head east on 94, and turn south on to [Conner Street](https://www.google.com/maps/place/42%C2%B023'40.5%22N+82%C2%B059'08.6%22W/@42.3945919,-82.987923,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x0:0x0!8m2!3d42.394588!4d-82.985729) (check out the google maps street view for yourself). Honestly, I was a privileged white kid who had never seen this kind of crap. I was absolutely shit-faced when I saw this crap and was terrified because we were driving a nice car, were dressed nice, and had a lot of party-related gifts in the back of the SUV -- we were a prime target for a robbing.

The most amazing part of the story is that, as we're traveling East on Jefferson Ave., the entire place is just a shit-storm of shit-skins. Every building is boarded up, and places where there would obviously be buildings if humans were in charge were just empty lots. As we were approaching Grosse Point, we saw [4 cop cars dealing with a situation at a gas station just before the entrance to GP.](https://www.google.com/maps/place/14910+E+Jefferson+Ave,+Detroit,+MI+48215/@42.3748895,-82.9399895,19z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m13!1m7!3m6!1s0x0:0x0!2zNDLCsDIzJzQwLjUiTiA4MsKwNTknMDguNiJX!3b1!8m2!3d42.394588!4d-82.985729!3m4!1s0x8824d5a8787a65df:0xc4afb01d244adac3!8m2!3d42.3748742!4d-82.9394872)

In light of this latest Reddit scandal, Voat should be drawing in a lot more newcomers. The biggest barrier it faces seems to be its public image.

Whenever Voat comes up on Reddit, someone will inevitably mention [this](https://www.reddit.com/r/videos/comments/4lmfmj/ceo_of_reddit_steve_huffman_about_advertising_on/d3orpmf). There's a [perfectly valid explanation](https://www.reddit.com/r/videos/comments/4lmfmj/ceo_of_reddit_steve_huffman_about_advertising_on/d3oo29y) for it, but that isn't what most visitors to the site will consider first and foremost when the top-rated comment on a front page news story is about how a reader knew it would be a nigger before he clicked on the article.

I'm *not* advocating for censorship, not even for comments such as those. Reddit has shown the final result of such efforts. But I do suggest that Voat could benefit from subverses with stricter rules that would make the site more inviting to newcomers. For every current sub, there could be another one with a different URL that forbids racial epithets and the like, and users could subscribe to that one if they prefer.

Unfettered expression is necessary for honest discourse, but its results don't always make for the best advertising. If we really want Voat to someday be a serious competitor for the likes of Reddit, we need to set up some special accommodations.
Kinder, gentler subverses to accompany (not replace!) the current ones.
